name: On the Biology of a Large Language Model (Anthropic)
oneLine: Anthropic's interpretability paper on Claude 3.5 Haiku: a hand-drawn circuit-diagram card grid opening a dense, figure-led long read.

palette.note: Warm off-white hero band behind the title and case-study grid; the reading area below is pure white
Parchment fill on the stacked 'feature' node boxes in every circuit diagram (capital, state, Dallas...)
Body copy at rgba(0,0,0,0.8); the title and card titles go to full #000000
Deep oxblood-brown on diagram edges, arrows and the dark 'Induction Head' nodes (sampled from the screenshot)

type.note: Title around 48px bold with tight negative tracking, sentence case; it wraps to 3 lines at about 64px on mobile
17px regular on about 29px leading over a 700px measure; italics mark terms such as 'attribution graphs'; underlined links in the same charcoal
Card titles 13-14px semibold in black; sidebar TOC 13px semibold for chapters and regular grey for appendices
12-13px, used inside diagrams for token strings ("rabbit", "habit", chain-of-thought transcripts)

layout: The hero is a centered 1180px block: the title, a 2-line dek, then a 6x2 grid of 180x245px cards. Each card is a square diagram thumbnail over a white caption area, with a 1px light-grey border and no shadow.

Below the hero the paper switches to a sticky left table of contents (about 300px wide, behind a hairline divider) and a 700px reading column starting at x=368, with footnote and citation markers inline in small blue.

The text is dense but well spaced: about 16px between paragraphs, indented bulleted case-study lists with bold underlined lead-ins, and § section numbering that doubles as link text ('§ 16 Related Work').
motion: (inferred) Almost no ambient motion: 62 inline SVGs and 0 canvas or video elements suggest static diagrams that become interactive on hover or click, not animated ones.
(inferred) Hovering a hero card most likely lifts or outlines it before it jumps to its section anchor. The stacked 'paper' offset on each node box already gives the diagrams depth without animation.
(inferred) The interactive attribution-graph figures deeper in the paper highlight connected nodes and edges on hover, so the motion is state change rather than scripted animation.
interactions: The case-study card grid works as visual navigation: each card links to its chapter, so the hero doubles as the table of contents.
The sticky sidebar TOC tracks reading position across a very long paper and splits chapters (bold) from appendices (grey).
Footnote and citation markers ([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) open inline hovercards instead of sending readers to the bottom of the page.
steal: Research landing hero: a grid of findings cards, each with a mini diagram of the anomaly mechanism (a channel spike, drift, or correlated failure across subsystems) that links to its deep-dive section.
Pipeline/architecture section: a node-and-edge diagram language with stacked offset 'feature' boxes, one neutral fill, and one accent color reserved for the path that triggered the anomaly flag.
Long-form methods page: a sticky left TOC with a bold-to-grey hierarchy (core sections vs. appendix: data prep, ESA dataset notes, eval details) next to a roughly 700px reading column.
leave: The warm parchment-and-oxblood palette is tied to Anthropic's identity and reads as cozy and print-like. Our telemetry site should feel colder and more mission-control.
The 17px-on-700px wall of text works for peer researchers but will lose recruiters. Lead with visuals and keep the full prose behind a 'read the method' depth layer.
